title: Pilot milestone ops & benchmarking playbook - Saturn Health
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark runbook, sample prompts, and secure upload instructions by 2025-12-06
Saturn to provide 2 weeks of anonymized traffic profile and top-3 success prompts by 2025-12-10
Agree exec readout date for week of 2026-01-27 and invite execs from product and infra
action_items: Lena Morales: send benchmark runbook, upload S3 instructions, and sample eval set (due 2025-12-06)
Dmitri Ivanov: prepare Dedicated vs Hosted perf config and example infra templates (due 2025-12-08)
Priya Natarajan: provide traffic logs, QPS distribution, and 3 golden prompts (due 2025-12-10)
Jamal Ortiz: share required security controls (KMS/HSM, VPC peering, audit scope) and SSO metadata (due 2025-12-09)
Marcus Lee: create IAM role and temp creds for Redwood test cluster, add network contact (due 2025-12-07)
header: Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Dmitri (Redwood SE), Priya (Saturn Head of AI), Marcus (Platform), Jamal (Security), Ava (Product)
summary: Goal: agree POC milestones, access plan, benchmark criteria and timeline for pilot evaluating Redwood inference for chat + retrieval workloads
Scope: baseline perf vs current infra, quality on held-out prompts, security gating for VPC/on-prem requirements
Success criteria: p95 latency target, throughput target, cost threshold and quality delta vs baseline
Timeline: kickoff immediately, access & dataset by week 1, mid-point review after 2 weeks of runs, exec readout end of month 7-week window
topics: Workload sizing: QPS, avg tokens, concurrency
Milestones: mid-point review, failover tests, exec readout
transcript: 00:00 Lena: Okay thanks everyone for joining, um this is Lena from Redwood — I'll kick us off. We have about 55 minutes. Does the time still work?
00:07 Priya: Yep all good, thanks. Priya here — Head of AI at Saturn. We've got Marcus, Jamal and Ava on as well.

00:15 Marcus: Hi all — quick note, we want a pragmatic pilot not a huge lift, main ask is can you show us the perf delta and ops overhead for switching to Redwood, especially for our retrieval-chat flows.

00:28 Lena: Perfect. Quick intros — Dmitri is our SE and will help with the runbook and infra questions. We'll outline milestones: kickoff, access, bench runs, mid-point review, exec readout. Sound ok?
00:40 Dmitri: Hi — yeah I'll own the perf config and will prepare a hosted vs dedicated template so you can see tradeoffs.
00:48 Ava: Quick ask — we care about 95th percentile latency under 400ms for the short chat path, and quality no worse than 3% below our current model on our eval set.
00:57 Priya: Also cost per 1k tokens is a gating factor; we have an internal target we'd like to be under but can share offline.
01:06 Lena: Cool. We'll capture those as success criteria — p95 latency < 400ms, quality delta < 3% vs baseline, and target unit cost threshold (TBD by Saturn).
01:18 Jamal: For security we need: SOC2 report, KMS/HSM controls, VPC peering or private link, and SSO/SAML metadata. Also logs must be retained for 90 days.
01:30 Dmitri: We can provide SOC2 attestation and support VPC peering for Redwood Private; for Hosted we can discuss field-level encryption and customer-managed keys. I'll list exact artifacts.

01:45 Marcus: On infra, our current stack is EKS + a sidecar for embeddings, plus an inference ensemble running on SageMaker. Typical traffic right now is ~600 RPS at peak with a 95th of about 700ms — so the 400ms is aggressive but achievable for optimized paths.
02:05 Priya: To be clear, 'chat short path' = user prompt + retrieval + 1 shot generation; avg tokens per request ~ 180, but we have long form flows too (avg 800 tokens). We'll want to test both.
02:20 Lena: Good detail. For workload sizing we'll need QPS distribution, token histogram, and an example spike pattern. Marcus can you share two weeks of anonymized traffic?
02:30 Marcus: Yes we can, will strip PII and send as gzipped logs.

02:36 Lena: Great. Now the milestone timeline proposal: Kickoff this week (access & dataset), Week 1: get infra creds & sample uploads, Week 2: run initial perf matrix (latency/throughput), Week 3: iterate on batching + quantization, Mid-point review at end of week 3, and Exec readout week 7. Does that align?
02:55 Priya: That seems reasonable — want to make sure mid-point shows both perf numbers and quality regressions so execs are comfortable.
03:05 Dmitri: We'll include both system metrics and quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE not great for chat, so we'll use an eval accuracy and preference rate with your golden prompts).
03:18 Ava: Can you explain what the mid-point deliverable will look like? Slides? Raw results?

03:23 Dmitri: Mid-point will be a short readout: runbook summary, perf matrix (p50/p95/p99), cost estimate, and quality delta against golden set. We'll attach raw CSVs and a short log playback for failures.
03:40 Jamal: On access — we prefer temporary IAM roles with scoped permissions and no long-term keys. Also need network contact for VPC peering if you go Redwood Private.
03:50 Lena: Noted. Marcus and Jamal we'll coordinate for role creation. Dmitri will send a template for IAM policies and the minimal network ports required.
04:00 Marcus: One more: Do you require any agent or collector in our cluster? We try to avoid installing anything that persists.

04:08 Dmitri: For Hosted there's no permanent agent — we ask for an ephemeral upload of a sample dataset or a short-term peered connection. For Private, we can run in your VPC with no outbound traffic depending on the setup. We'll document both options.
04:25 Priya: Benchmarks — what are you measuring exactly? Latency, tokens/sec, cost, and... quality?

04:31 Dmitri: Precisely: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput at target concurrency, cost per 1k tokens for the workload mix, and quality pass-rate on the golden set. We'll also run degradation tests (model fallback to cheaper variants) and autoscaling behavior under spike.

04:50 Lena: We'll propose two benchmark tracks: 1) Short chat path (low tokens) focusing on latency, 2) Long-form (high tokens) focusing on throughput and cost. Both will include retrieval + generation integrated runs.
05:05 Ava: For quality metrics, can we include a human-preference check? We can do a small AMT batch or internal raters.
05:11 Priya: We prefer internal raters — we'll define 200 preference pairs for the pilot.
05:16 Dmitri: Perfect, we'll include instructions for creating blind eval pairs and a scoring rubric.

06:00 Lena: Access checklist we'll need: a) temp IAM role with S3 write/read for a bucket we use for uploads, b) optional VPC peering request if you want Redwood Private, c) SSO metadata if you want to use SAML for console access, d) audit log retention requirements.
06:18 Jamal: We'll aim to provide IAM role and SSO metadata by Monday. For VPC peering we'll need a security review but can start the paperwork.
07:02 Marcus: About Dedicated vs Hosted — can you summarize tradeoffs quickly?

07:07 Dmitri: Short version: Hosted = fastest time-to-value, Redwood manages infra, some constraints on private networking; Dedicated = reserved GPUs in our infra with performance isolation and predictable latency; Private = runs in your VPC or on-prem, greatest control but more setup. For perf, Dedicated tends to hit better p95s due to isolated pools and pinned models.
07:35 Priya: For our compliance we might need Private eventually, but for the pilot Hosted with encrypt-in-flight + CMK could work if we limit data uploaded.
07:46 Lena: We'll provision a Hosted pilot with options to run a Dedicated comparison. Dmitri will prepare a cost/latency comparison matrix for the exact Saturn traffic profile.
08:10 Ava: Bench runs — are you going to use our retrieval infra or Redwood's? We use a custom vector store — Milvus on EKS.

08:20 Dmitri: Ideally we run end-to-end using your retrieval to ensure network and retrieval latency included. If you prefer we can run both: local retrieval + synthetic retrieval to isolate generator latency.
09:01 Marcus: We'll do end-to-end. Expect retrieval cold-starts that add ~120ms sometimes.
09:10 Priya: Also want to test prefix caching / KV cache behavior for long-session flows, how does Redwood handle KV cache on repeated user sessions?

09:20 Dmitri: Redwood runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache management; note in some transcripts 'KV cache' gets transcribed as 'K-V cash' — sorry, audio joke. But technically we can enable per-session KV caching and measure hit-rate. For the pilot we'll instrument cache hit-rate as a metric.
09:45 Jamal: Regarding auditing — we need access logs, token-level metadata for 90 days, and the ability to export logs to our SIEM. Can Redwood push logs to a customer S3 or do we need a connector?
09:58 Dmitri: We can push logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket or stream via Kinesis/CloudWatch subscription; we'll include both options in the runbook.

10:30 Lena: Let's lock down the success criteria verbatim: (1) p95 latency < 400ms on short chat path; (2) throughput to sustain 600RPS with <10% error; (3) quality delta less than 3% on golden prompts; (4) operational controls validated (IAM, VPC or CMK, logs). Is that acceptable?
10:48 Priya: Yes — though we'll add a cost target line item after we share internal thresholds.
11:00 Marcus: One operational test — we want a failover demonstration: if the primary model is overloaded, can you automatically route to a cheaper fallback within SLO?
11:09 Dmitri: Yes we have smart routing policies and fallbacks; we'll include a short failover test in the mid-point so you can see behavior and user impact.
12:00 Ava: For the exec readout what should we prepare?
12:05 Lena: Short slide deck: objective, methodology, perf & cost results, recommendations, and next steps. Keep it to 10 slides. We will co-author it and present jointly.
12:25 Priya: I want to make sure product and infra execs are represented so they can sign off on Dedicated or Private if we go that route.
12:33 Lena: We'll request attendee list when scheduling the readout. Now any blockers left?
12:40 Jamal: Only security paperwork; we'll start the intake now. Also need to confirm what data leaves the VPC for Hosted tests.
12:48 Dmitri: We'll specify data flows; for Hosted tests we can limit to anonymized payloads and optional field-level encryption. For Private tests nothing leaves your network unless you opt-in.
13:05 Marcus: Ok timeline recap please — I want dates on the calendar.

13:10 Lena: Proposed dates: Kickoff week of 2025-12-08, access & uploads by 2025-12-12, baseline runs 12/15-12/19, iterative tuning week 12/22-12/26, mid-point review 2026-01-08 (week after holidays), exec readout week of 2026-01-27. We can compress if Saturn wants quicker cadence.
13:35 Priya: Mid-Jan is okay. Please factor in our holiday freeze — 12/24-01/02 we are low capacity, so runs before that are preferred.
14:00 Lena: We'll adjust to run heavier tests prior to 12/22. Dmitri will shift the schedule and share a detailed milestone calendar.
14:20 Dmitri: I'll also include a short troubleshooting runbook: what to check if p95 spikes (batching, long tail tokens, network jitter, retrieval latency).
14:40 Ava: Can Redwood provide sample telemetry dashboards? We want to see token-level cost, p95 by route, and cache hit rates.
14:48 Dmitri: Yes — sample Grafana dashboards and a Prometheus scrape config will be attached.
15:10 Priya: One more question — do you support quantized model variants out-of-the-box? We want to trade accuracy for cost on long-form flows.
15:18 Dmitri: We support multiple quantization profiles and will recommend which to try per workload. We'll include a guidance doc and expected perf delta numbers.
16:05 Marcus: For the benchmark runs, what kind of synthetic load generator do you use?
16:12 Dmitri: We use a JMeter-based hook with request shaping to emulate your token distribution; but we can also accept your exact log playback for the most realistic test.

16:30 Lena: Alright — last part: communications and owners. I'll be the AE owner, Dmitri is SE owner for the runbook. Priya and Marcus are Saturn owners. We'll assign the action items after the call. Any final comments?
16:47 Priya: No, thanks everyone — looking forward to the runbook.
16:52 Jamal: Thanks, please share the security artifact list.
16:56 Lena: Will do. We'll follow up with the runbook and calendar invites. Meeting adjourned.
54:30 [call ended]
